title: Environment Accommodations
description: Accommodations affecting the physical and structural classroom environment. Use when the student needs reduced distraction, structured seating, modified physical access, or a calmer setting to access instruction.

source.name: ADayInOurShoes — Ultimate List of IEP Accommodations, Modifications & Strategies (SDIs)
source.section: IEP accommodations and strategies for environment

accommodations.text: A quiet area to complete the work or take a test.
Having someone read a test to them.
Preferential seating: sitting near the front, away from distraction, or in their area of preference (if they prefer a left or right visual field).
Preferential seating away from distractions, windows, doors, and speakers.
Extra time to complete the work or reading given.
Early dismissal from class to get to locker and to next class.

A 'hot pass' or 'cool off card' the student can flash to the teacher to leave class and go to a designated person (office, guidance counselor, nurse) to cool off if they feel a negative behavior coming on.
High contrast materials and limited visual clutter.
Adapted lunch setting to reduce sensory stressors.
Adapted recess with adult-led activities to increase peer interactions.
Recess and group activities designed with IEP goals in mind.
Access to resource room or learning support room.
